Sometimes it’s all I can say.  I just have to accept this moment, this situation, I can’t rush through it so I just have to exist through it. What an honor and a struggle it is to exist through it. And what else is there I can do? So I say “ok” and accept it. Accept the circumstance, or the calling, or the end, the uncertainty, hardship, frustration of it all.  Things outside my control, but that obviously affect me, so what more is there to do or say than grin and bear it?  There’s a reason I have to embrace it this way, a purpose for why I’m forced into this position. Somehow life finds a Wah to turn me into a carnival contortionist and twists my soul to fit this path I’m on.  Just trying to take it in, to take it on, to get through it.  Sending love to everyone who feels similar right now, sometimes we just need people to believe in us. I believe in you. You’ve got this.  #1924us #life #animation #mrskelly #fyp

Meme history - Okay Let's Go! or OK Let's Go refers to a viral video and meme of an amusement park ride enthusiast that went viral in the Netherlands in 2014 after a TV show grouped two Turbo Polyp fans (one younger and one older) with the kid showing a miniature version of the ride who says, "ok let's go," which subsequently became a memorable catchphrase said by the ride's operator. The video was first posted to YouTube in 2014 and was reposted as a meme in mid-2020, with a green-screened edit spreading in August 2023 to TikTok, leading to subsequent exploitable image macro memes in which the teen would be positioned in random places with a coinciding caption related to the start of something new. Origin - On June 20th, 2009, a Dutch TV show aired an episode dedicated to Maikel Van Hoof, a man who loves amusement parks and the Turbo Polyp ride. The video uploaded to YouTube by user @FlyLo123, garnered over 962,000 views and 4,500 likes in 14 years. The interview became a popular meme Netherlands and, five years later, the same TV show decided to do another episode about Van Hoof's obsession with the Turbo Polyp ride. This time, however, they brought a teen who was also an enthusiast of the amusement park ride. In one particular moment of the program, the teen holds a mic and says "Okay Let's Go!", which is a catchphrase commonly said by Maikel Van Hoof and the Turbo Polyp's operators. The interview was uploaded on YouTube on January 29th, 2014, by user @kermistube, amassing more than 4.9 million views and 80,000 likes in nine years.
